main_text.l: cire, usurpatâ sibi authoritate militem conscribere, inexpertum Regis animum à proceribus alienare, illos vicissim in Principem suum concitare: his denique luxum ad invidiæ summam conjungere, unâ subinde noctè aureorum trecenta, & amplius miilia per aleam & convivia prodigere. Horum jam sæpiùs criminum coram Rege à Dynastis insimulatus, qui, ut optimus etiam fuisset, zelo tamen frendebant hominis & peregrini & novi; sciverat nihilominus callidum & vivax ingenium, speciosis erga Regem suum obsequiis, criminationes iftas diluere. Sed invalescentibus adversariis, & indies invidiâ crescente, ajunt tandem sensisse Regem, ab insidiis irrequieti hominis, ne capiti quidem suo satis tutum esse: Proinde Vitrio præsidiariorum suorum duci mandat,

page.notes: The text is in italic-free roman with long s printed as s; the first line begins mid-word ("cire") as a continuation from the previous page. Right-edge fragments are show-through from the facing page and are omitted. Possible misreadings: "miilia" and "Rcgem" are as printed.
